title: Indian Army Officer Recruitment 2026: Entry Routes
metaDescription: Indian Army officer recruitment 2026: NDA, CDS and technical entry routes, age limits, SSB interview stages, and training at IMA Dehradun and OTA Chennai.
headline: How to Become an Indian Army Officer in 2026

sections.title: Entry routes
sections.content:
The main routes to an Indian Army commission are the National Defence Academy (NDA) after school, the Combined Defence Services (CDS) exam after graduation, the Technical Entry Scheme (TES) for engineering aspirants, and the NCC Special Entry for certificate holders. University graduates can also enter through the Short Service Commission, while technical graduates have dedicated technical entries.

NDA cadets train jointly with future Navy and Air Force officers before moving to the Indian Military Academy, while CDS entrants go directly to the IMA or the Officers Training Academy. Each route has its own notification cycle, published on the UPSC and Indian Army recruitment websites, so check the current notification rather than relying on last year's dates.

sections.title: Age limits and eligibility
sections.content:
NDA applicants must be between 16½ and 19½ years old, while CDS applicants are generally between 19 and 25 years old depending on the academy chosen. Candidates must meet nationality, education, and medical standards, and unmarried status is required for NDA and most CDS entries at the time of application.

Educational requirements vary by route: NDA requires passing Class 12, with physics and mathematics for the Air Force and Navy wings, while CDS requires a bachelor's degree, with specific subjects for some academies. Medical standards cover vision, hearing, height, weight, and general fitness, and are applied strictly at the military hospital stage.

sections.title: The SSB interview
sections.content:
The Services Selection Board (SSB) interview runs for five days and tests intelligence, personality, leadership, and teamwork. Stage one screens candidates with reasoning tests and picture-perception tests, and only those who clear it proceed to stage two.

Stage two includes psychological tests, group discussions, group planning exercises, outdoor group tasks, and a personal interview, ending with a conference of all assessors. Candidates recommended by the board then undergo medical examination, and final selection depends on merit position and available vacancies.

sections.title: Training and career
sections.content:
Training at the Indian Military Academy lasts about 18 months, while the Officers Training Academy course for Short Service Commission runs about 11 months. Cadets study tactics, weapons, physical training, leadership, and military law, with regular field exercises that test endurance and decision-making under pressure.

On successful completion, cadets are commissioned as Lieutenants and posted to regiments across the Army's combat arms, combat support arms, and services. Officers can rise through Captain, Major, Lieutenant Colonel, and beyond, with opportunities for staff courses, foreign postings, and specialist qualifications over a long career.

Each route leads to training at the Indian Military Academy in Dehradun or the Officers Training Academy in Chennai.
